newsitem.title: UK: Brand valuation offers role to ad agencies - study.
newsitem.headline: Brand valuation offers role to ad agencies - study.

text.p: Brand valuation, an accounting measure pioneered in the 1980s, is set to become more widespread, and advertising agencies are well-placed to advise companies on how to value their brands, according to a study released on Thursday.

"Like it or not, brand valuation looks certain to become more widely used in the future," David Haigh, managing director of the consultancy group Brand Finance Ltd, said in his study, "Brand Valuation: A Review of Current Practice".

Brand valuation was adopted by some companies in the 1980s as an accounting tool that boosted the value of balance sheets and was expected to provide protection against corporate raiders who targeted brand-rich companies.

Brand valuation was particularly attractive for British companies because brand valuations in Britain could be stated at cost in the balance sheet, did not have to be amortised and were subject only to annual review and confirmation of the carrying value by the directors, Haigh said.

The use of brand valuation continues to be hotly debated, but Haigh noted that various brand valuation techniques are now widely accepted by auditors, courts, tax authorities, merchant bankers, investment analysts and general managers.
"Given the rapid development and growing acceptance of brand valuation techniques, it is important to consider how brand valuation is likely to impact on advertising agencies," he said.

Advertising agencies' intimate knowledge of the history of brands and the markets in which they operate, as well as their access to market research and media data make them particularly well placed to play a role in helping companies value their brands, Haigh said.

"Agencies need to retain the commercial high ground with their clients by understanding the new financial techniques being used," Haigh said. "Better still they should become experts in their own right, leading client thinking or contributing to the process as an equal partner."
